newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Loe tipped to return to Waikato.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Loe tipped to return to Waikato.

text.p: HAMILTON, Nov 21 - Prop Richard Loe is tipped to return to Waikato and play his Super 12 rugby for the Chiefs, NZPA reported on Thursday.
Sources indicate the 36-year-old former All Black test prop has been snapped up by Waikato Chiefs coach Brad Meurant after being dumped by the Canterbury Crusaders.
The powerhouse forward played 96 games for Waikato until 1994 -- but was vilified for infamous incidents involving Otago fullback Greg Cooper and Wallaby winger Paul Carozza.
He showed he possessed immense mauling and scrummaging skills when Canterbury beat Waikato in the last game of this year's national provincial championships at Rugby Park last month.

The Chiefs have limited propping options and are understood to have looked outside their catchment area for at least two of the front row positions for next year's competition, which begins on February 28.
Meurant confirmed he was interested in Loe after Crusaders' coach Wayne Smith told the veteran front-rower he was not wanted following the signing of Auckland's Kevin Nepia.
Loe anchored Canterbury Crusaders' front row this year as well as captaining the team.
Loe believed he had been axed because of his age, but Meurant said that wasn't a problem.
"Whether players are 14 or 40 -- it doesn't matter to me as long as they can do the job."
Rival Chiefs propping prospect Murray Driver was less than thrilled to hear Loe was looking to move.
"It is not a great thing for me that Richard is on the loose," Driver said.
"On experience he can't be beaten, but I guess it depends what selectors are looking for."
Smith said Loe was great for his tight game in the scrums and mauls, but he was looking for more mobility in his front row.
